title: Psalm 19 — The skies recount the glory of El, and the law of YHWH

verdicts.reasoning: lamnaṣṣēaḥ mizmôr lĕdāwid = MT v 1; MT 19:n = ASV 19:(n-1) verified; the canon cites 'XIX-5', 'XIX-7' in MT numbering. Exact.

citations: Kraus, Psalms 1-59, ad loc. (El in vv 2-7)
verdicts.reasoning: haššāmayim mĕsappĕrîm kĕbôd-ʾēl ûmaʿăśēh yādāyw maggîd hārāqîaʿ: 'skies' (physical, vv 3-7), 'El' (extended shaddai-eloah; the El/YHWH split of the two halves is preserved), 'the dome' (central raqia, inferred, with ASV 'firmament' recorded). Each choice is a recorded corpus convention; none adds content.
yôm lĕyôm yabbîaʿ ʾōmer wĕlaylâ lĕlaylâ yĕḥawweh-dāʿat: Hiphil nbʿ 'pour forth'; Piel ḥwh. Exact.
ʾên-ʾōmer wĕʾên dĕbārîm bĕlî nišmāʿ qôlām: three negations (ASV, NRSV); the KJV relative construal is recorded and rightly rejected. Exact.

bĕkol-hāʾāreṣ yāṣāʾ qawwām ... laššemeš śām-ʾōhel bāhem: MT qaw 'line' and bāhem 'in them' kept; LXX phthongos and the emendation bayyām recorded. The reception note correctly says the canon's 'sur la mer' rests on the emendation, not the MT. Exact and source-honest.
wĕhûʾ kĕḥātān yōṣēʾ mēḥuppātô yāśîś kĕgibbôr lārûṣ ʾōraḥ. Exact.
miqṣēh haššāmayim môṣāʾô ûtĕqûpātô ʿal-qĕṣôtām: 'circuit' (tĕqûpâ, ASV), not the canon's 'orbite'; the line renders the horizon-to-horizon image. Lens-free.
tôrat YHWH tĕmîmâ mĕšîbat nāpeš ...: ASV Torah set, one English word per term; nepeš 'soul' as the self restored (overlay). Exact.
piqqûdê YHWH yĕšārîm ... miṣwat YHWH bārâ mĕʾîrat ʿênāyim. Exact.
yirʾat YHWH ṭĕhôrâ ʿômedet lāʿad mišpĕṭê-YHWH ʾĕmet ṣādĕqû yaḥdāw: MT yirʾat kept (no textual support for ʾimrat). Exact.
hanneḥĕmādîm mizzāhāb ûmippaz rāb ûmĕtûqîm middĕbaš wĕnōpet ṣûpîm. Exact; no lexical decision.
gam-ʿabdĕkā nizhār bāhem bĕšomrām ʿēqeb rāb: 'is warned'; 'great reward'. Exact.
gam mizzēdîm ḥăśōk ʿabdekā ...: abstract 'presumptuous sins' (ASV) with 'the insolent' recorded; ʾêtām from tmm. Exact.
yihyû lĕrāṣôn ʾimrê-pî wĕhegyôn libbî lĕpāneykā YHWH ṣûrî wĕgōʾălî. Exact.

glossaryReview.reasoning: Philologically neutral and correctly direct: a typographic convention, with the Hebrew form standing in the source text and every name verified (David, Solomon, Jerusalem, Zion, Israel, Jacob, Job). Flagged only because it is founder point D (the corpus split with the Kings transliteration). Reviewer view: accept English forms for the Writings. Job 37 must match the stable job-woh chapters, which are not retro-edited, and the four books must agree with each other. Record the genre split (narrative transliterated, poetry English) as deliberate, or settle it corpus-wide in one later decision.

Every site verified: YHWH; 'Yah' (Ps 147:1, 20); the article follows the Hebrew (anarthrous Ps 8:6; Eccl 3:10, 13; articular Eccl 3:11, 14, 15, 17, 18); 'El', 'Eloah' and 'Shaddai' as in stable job-woh (38:41; 40:2, 9); 'our Lord' for ʾădōnênû. Direct is right: these are presentation rules over explicit Hebrew forms. Flagged only for founder point A (Ps 8:6 'Elohim' against the canon's 'the Elohim'). Reviewer view: keep the anarthrous form. The Hebrew has no article, the rule matches job-woh 1:9 and the Kings clause 2, and departing from the canon's wording here is evidence that the line is not canon-driven.

Site-by-site application of the founder's Kings-wave register ruling, checked verse by verse: physical sky 'skies' (Ps 8:2, 4, 9; 19:2, 7; 33:6; 147:8; Prov 8:27; Eccl 3:1; Job 37:3); dwelling or cosmic height 'heavens' (Ps 33:13 || mĕkôn-šibtô; 139:8 against She'ol). Ps 8:2 ('splendor upon the skies') is the closest call and is argued from v 4. Direct is appropriate.

'earth' at universal and cosmic sites (kol-hāʾāreṣ; ʾereṣ || tēbēl) is the reading of ASV, NRSV and NJPS, and the isaiah-woh precedent. 'land' is kept for territory (Prov 10:30; Job 37:13) and the stable 'wings of the land' (Job 37:3 = 38:13). Every site was checked. Agree with founder point C: promote the clause to central eretz in a later diff.

citations: Wolff, Anthropology of the Old Testament (1974), ch. 2
glossaryReview.reasoning: The 'life' / 'soul' split was checked at all six sites. 'life' where a life is delivered from death or forfeited (Ps 33:19 || 'keep them alive'; Prov 8:36 in the life/death antithesis), as in the Kings and Ezekiel overlays. ASV 'soul' is kept for the self (Ps 19:8; 33:20; 139:14; Prov 10:3), with the appetite sense in commentary. Direct is defensible: BDB lists both senses.

Applied correctly at every listed site. MT Psalm numbering was verified (superscription = v 1 in Pss 8, 19; run into v 1 in Ps 139). The one vowel-only exception at Ps 8:2 is declared and justified: the MT impv. tĕnâ has no syntax after ʾăšer. Eccl 3:21 keeps the Masoretic articular participles and fully records the interrogative reading of LXX, Vulgate, ASV, NRSV and NJPS. Non-blocking: add 'KJV' to the Eccl 3:21 clause as the English witness to the MT pointing ('the spirit of man that goeth upward'), so that the entry does not suggest that every English version departs from the MT.
The ASV terms are accurate, and the uncertainty is honestly stated: lamnaṣṣēaḥ (Piel ptc. nṣḥ), mizmôr, Gittith, and the ambiguity of lĕdāwid. Direct is appropriate.
Six terms, six English words (ASV); MT yirʾat is kept against the unsupported ʾimrat emendation. The 'law'/'teaching' corpus reconciliation is correctly deferred.

Append-only (verified). It extends the stable job-woh practice for bare ʾēl ('El', 38:41; 40:9) to Job 37 and to Ps 19:2; 139:17, 23, and 'Eloah' to Ps 139:19, and it names the isaiah-woh 'God' exception explicitly. All appliesTo sites were checked against the Hebrew.

The report's list of the three canon-coincident lines (section 1) confirmed the two commentary revisions: at Job 37:18 and Prov 8:30 the notes cite only the canon's French, whose wording matches the line, and omit the canon's English ('the sky'; 'as one brought up with him'), which does not. founderDecisionRecommendations.A-Ps-8:6-article-on-Elohim: Keep 'a little less than Elohim' without the article. The Hebrew mēʾĕlōhîm is anarthrous, the rule matches job-woh 1:9 and Kings clause 2, and the reception note already gives the canon's 'the Elohim'. Differing from the canon here is useful evidence that the line follows the Hebrew.
founderDecisionRecommendations.B-bene-(ha)adam: Accept 'the sons of the human' / 'the sons of human' for coherence with central ha-adam / ben-adam and GEN-WOH-11:5, and align 1 Kgs 8:39 ('the children of men') to it. The cost is stiff English at Prov 8:4, 31, and the Hebrew article on bĕnê (hā)ʾādām carries no difference in sense. If the founder prefers idiom, revert every plural site together to 'the sons of men' (string swap; drop the plural refIds from the ha-adam and ben-adam ops). Do not mix the two.

founderDecisionRecommendations.D-proper-names: Accept English forms in the four Writings books. Job 37 must match the stable job-woh chapters, and the four books must agree. Record the corpus practice as genre-split (narrative transliterated, poetry and prophets English) or settle it in one corpus-wide decision. Do not leave it implicit.
founderDecisionRecommendations.E-chesed-kindness: Confirm 'kindness' for solitary ḥesed now, before the Psalter grows (about 120 occurrences). It is the central wohChoice, consistent with genesis-woh and Kings, and lexically sound (Glueck; Sakenfeld). The loyalty sense stays in commentary, and the fixed pair ḥesed wĕʾĕmet stays under chesed-v-emet.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F-Job-37:18-clouds: No decision needed: 'clouds' rests on BDB/HALOT, KJV and stable job-woh 38:37, and 'strong' (not 'solid') keeps the line neutral. i18n.en: For the Chief Musician. A Psalm of David.

notes.official: Superscription, counted as v 1 in the Masoretic numbering, so MT 19:n = ASV 19:(n-1) throughout (MT 19:15 = ASV 19:14; `mt-baseline-versification-and-psalm-numbering-writings`). The canon cites the psalm in the MT numbering ('Psaumes XIX-5', 'XIX-7'), which matches the refIds. Superscription terms as at Ps 8:1 (`psalm-superscription-terms-psalms`).

paragraphs.text: הַשָּׁמַ֗יִם מְֽסַפְּרִ֥ים כְּבֽוֹד־אֵ֑ל וּֽמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָ֝דָ֗יו מַגִּ֥יד הָרָקִֽיעַ׃

i18n.en: The skies recount the glory of El, and the dome declares the work of his hands.

notes.official:
*haššāmayim mĕsappĕrîm kĕbôd-ʾēl* 'The skies recount the glory of El'. The participle *mĕsappĕrîm* is 'telling, recounting' (ASV 'declare'). *šāmayim* is the visible sky, which speaks by day and by night (vv 3-7), so 'skies' (central `shamayim`; ASV 'heavens'). *ʾēl* is transliterated 'El', as in job-woh (central `shaddai-eloah`, extended in this wave to bare *ʾēl* in the poetic books; ASV 'God'). *hārāqîaʿ* 'the dome' applies the central `raqia` entry (ASV 'firmament'). The pair *šāmayim* / *rāqîaʿ* is the pair of Gen 1:8, where the *rāqîaʿ* is named *šāmayim*.

The two halves of the psalm use different divine names: *ʾēl* once in the creation hymn (vv 2-7), YHWH seven times in the Torah hymn (vv 8-15). The line keeps the distinction (`divine-names-convention-writings`).

paragraphs.text: י֣וֹם לְ֭יוֹם יַבִּ֣יעַֽ אֹ֑מֶר וְלַ֥יְלָה לְּ֝לַ֗יְלָה יְחַוֶּה־דָּֽעַת׃

i18n.en: Day to day pours forth speech, and night to night declares knowledge.

notes.official: *yabbîaʿ ʾōmer* 'pours forth speech' (Hiphil of *nbʿ* 'bubble up, gush'); *yĕḥawweh-dāʿat* 'declares knowledge' (Piel of *ḥwh*, an Aramaizing verb).

paragraphs.text: אֵֽין־אֹ֭מֶר וְאֵ֣ין דְּבָרִ֑ים בְּ֝לִ֗י נִשְׁמָ֥ע קוֹלָֽם׃

i18n.en: There is no speech, and there are no words; their voice is not heard.

notes.official: *ʾên-ʾōmer wĕʾên dĕbārîm bĕlî nišmāʿ qôlām* 'There is no speech, and there are no words; their voice is not heard' (ASV; NRSV likewise). The clauses are three negations: the testimony of the sky is wordless. The KJV construes 'There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard', which takes *bĕlî* as a relative and gives the opposite sense; the grammar favours the ASV reading.

paragraphs.text: בְּכָל־הָאָ֨רֶץ ׀ יָ֘צָ֤א קַוָּ֗ם וּבִקְצֵ֣ה תֵ֭בֵל מִלֵּיהֶ֑ם לַ֝שֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ שָֽׂם־אֹ֥הֶל בָּהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: Their line has gone out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world. For the sun he has set a tent in them,

notes.official:
*bĕkol-hāʾāreṣ yāṣāʾ qawwām* 'Their line has gone out through all the earth'. MT *qaw* is a measuring line (ASV 'line'). The LXX *phthongos* 'sound', quoted at Rom 10:18, is usually explained as a reading *qôlām* 'their voice' (NRSV). The line keeps the MT (`mt-baseline-versification-and-psalm-numbering-writings`). *bĕkol-hāʾāreṣ* || *biqṣēh tēbēl* 'to the end of the world' is universal, so 'earth' (`eretz-earth-and-land-scope-writings`).

*laššemeš śām-ʾōhel bāhem* 'For the sun he has set a tent in them': *bāhem* refers back to the skies of v 2. Some modern commentators emend to *bayyām* 'in the sea', where the sun sets and rises; the line follows the MT.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes the verse in a French wording that has the emended text ('il a dressé une tente sur la mer', 'he has set a tent upon the sea') and reads it as a further allusion to the mass of land created when the ocean covered the Earth, the original continent. The line renders the MT *bāhem* 'in them'. The emendation is recorded here and in the MT-baseline entry.

paragraphs.text: וְה֗וּא כְּ֭חָתָן יֹצֵ֣א מֵחֻפָּת֑וֹ יָשִׂ֥ישׂ כְּ֝גִבּ֗וֹר לָר֥וּץ אֹֽרַח׃

i18n.en: and he is like a bridegroom coming out of his chamber; he rejoices like a strong man to run his course.

notes.official: *kĕḥātān yōṣēʾ mēḥuppātô* 'like a bridegroom coming out of his chamber' (*ḥuppâ* 'canopy, bridal chamber'); *kĕgibbôr* 'like a strong man' (ASV), a warrior who runs his course.

paragraphs.text: מִקְצֵ֤ה הַשָּׁמַ֨יִם ׀ מֽוֹצָא֗וֹ וּתְקוּפָת֥וֹ עַל־קְצוֹתָ֑ם וְאֵ֥ין נִ֝סְתָּ֗ר מֵֽחַמָּתוֹ׃

i18n.en: His going forth is from the end of the skies, and his circuit to their ends, and nothing is hidden from his heat.

notes.official:
*miqṣēh haššāmayim môṣāʾô ûtĕqûpātô ʿal-qĕṣôtām* 'His going forth is from the end of the skies, and his circuit to their ends'. The idiom describes the sun's path from horizon to horizon, so *šāmayim* is the physical sky, 'skies' (central `shamayim`; ASV 'heavens'). *tĕqûpâ* is the turning or circuit of the sun or of the year (BDB; cf. Ex 34:22). *ḥammâ* 'heat' is also a poetic word for the sun itself (Isa 30:26).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes the verse ('his going forth is from the end of the heaven, and his circuit unto the ends of it'; French 'son orbite') and reads it as saying that the creators came from a planet very far from the Earth's orbit. The line renders the Hebrew image of the sun's daily course.

paragraphs.text: תּ֘וֹרַ֤ת יְהוָ֣ה תְּ֭מִימָה מְשִׁ֣יבַת נָ֑פֶשׁ עֵד֥וּת יְהוָ֥ה נֶ֝אֱמָנָ֗ה מַחְכִּ֥ימַת פֶּֽתִי׃

i18n.en: The law of YHWH is perfect, restoring the soul; the testimony of YHWH is sure, making wise the simple.

notes.official: The Torah hymn (vv 8-11) names YHWH's instruction six times with six terms: *tôrâ* 'law', *ʿēdût* 'testimony', *piqqûdîm* 'precepts', *miṣwâ* 'commandment', *yirʾâ* 'fear', *mišpāṭîm* 'ordinances'. The line keeps the ASV set, one English word for each Hebrew term (`torah-vocabulary-psalm-19`). *mĕšîbat nāpeš* 'restoring the soul' (ASV; NJPS 'renewing life'): *nepeš* here is the self, the whole person (`nefesh-scope-writings`). *maḥkîmat petî* 'making wise the simple'.

paragraphs.text: פִּקּ֘וּדֵ֤י יְהוָ֣ה יְ֭שָׁרִים מְשַׂמְּחֵי־לֵ֑ב מִצְוַ֥ת יְהוָ֥ה בָּ֝רָ֗ה מְאִירַ֥ת עֵינָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: The precepts of YHWH are right, rejoicing the heart; the commandment of YHWH is pure, enlightening the eyes.

notes.official: *piqqûdê YHWH* 'the precepts of YHWH' and *miṣwat YHWH* 'the commandment of YHWH' (`torah-vocabulary-psalm-19`). *bārâ* 'pure'; *mĕʾîrat ʿênāyim* 'enlightening the eyes'.

paragraphs.text: יִרְאַ֤ת יְהוָ֨ה ׀ טְהוֹרָה֮ עוֹמֶ֪דֶת לָ֫עַ֥ד מִֽשְׁפְּטֵי־יְהוָ֥ה אֱמֶ֑ת צָֽדְק֥וּ יַחְדָּֽו׃

i18n.en: The fear of YHWH is clean, enduring forever; the ordinances of YHWH are true, they are righteous altogether.

notes.official: *yirʾat YHWH* 'the fear of YHWH' stands in the series for the instruction that teaches reverence; the emendation *ʾimrat* 'the word of' has no textual support and is not adopted. *mišpĕṭê-YHWH* 'the ordinances of YHWH' (ASV); *ṣādĕqû yaḥdāw* 'they are righteous altogether' (`torah-vocabulary-psalm-19`).

paragraphs.text: הַֽנֶּחֱמָדִ֗ים מִ֭זָּהָב וּמִפַּ֣ז רָ֑ב וּמְתוּקִ֥ים מִ֝דְּבַ֗שׁ וְנֹ֣פֶת צוּפִֽים׃

i18n.en: More to be desired are they than gold, than much fine gold; sweeter also than honey and the drippings of the honeycomb.

paragraphs.text: גַּֽם־עַ֭בְדְּךָ נִזְהָ֣ר בָּהֶ֑ם בְּ֝שָׁמְרָ֗ם עֵ֣קֶב רָֽב׃

i18n.en: Moreover, by them your servant is warned; in keeping them there is great reward.
Errors — who can discern them? Clear me from hidden faults.

notes.official: *šĕgîʾôt* 'errors' are faults committed unknowingly (cf. Lev 4); *minnistārôt naqqēnî* 'Clear me from hidden faults'.

paragraphs.text: גַּ֤ם מִזֵּדִ֨ים ׀ חֲשֹׂ֬ךְ עַבְדֶּ֗ךָ אַֽל־יִמְשְׁלוּ־בִ֣י אָ֣ז אֵיתָ֑ם וְ֝נִקֵּ֗יתִי מִפֶּ֥שַֽׁע רָֽב׃

i18n.en: Keep back your servant also from presumptuous sins; let them not rule over me. Then I shall be blameless, and I shall be clear of great transgression.

notes.official: *mizzēdîm* 'from presumptuous sins' (ASV). Elsewhere *zēdîm* are 'the insolent' (Ps 119:21, 51), and some render 'from the arrogant'; the abstract sense suits the contrast with the unwitting errors of v 13 (BDB). *ʾêtām* 'I shall be blameless' (from *tmm*); *pešaʿ rāb* 'great transgression'.

paragraphs.text: יִֽהְי֥וּ לְרָצ֨וֹן ׀ אִמְרֵי־פִ֡י וְהֶגְי֣וֹן לִבִּ֣י לְפָנֶ֑יךָ יְ֝הוָ֗ה צוּרִ֥י וְגֹאֲלִֽי׃

i18n.en: Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before you, YHWH, my rock and my redeemer.

notes.official: *ṣûrî wĕgōʾălî* 'my rock and my redeemer': the *gōʾēl* is the kinsman who buys back a relative or his property (Lev 25:25; Ruth 4:1-6).
